text.p: A spokesman for nickel producer Eramet said the company was "surprised" by a government decision to expropriate a key mining licence in New Caledonia and "did not understand" the motives.
"Until a few days ago we have been negotiating on the basis of a swap between Koniambo and Poum," Eramet spokesman Alain Ray told Reuters.
"And then on Friday evening we receive a letter announcing the procedure of expropriation will be started," he added.
In the government statement, the Ministry of Industry said Eramet had not used the Koniambo mine since 1975.
"That is correct and very normal. A mining company does not use all mines at the same time, you keep reserves. The mining directorate (of the Industry Ministry) was kept informed," Ray said.
Eramet, which only has mines on New Caledonia and is the world third-biggest nickel producer, planned to start Koniambo again in 2008 and said it would be at full capacity in 2010.
"Koniambo represents 50 percent of our future nickel ore needs," he said.

Eramet plans to produce 60,000 to 65,000 tonnes of nickel per year after 2000 and any compensation for Koniambo would need to provide ore sufficient for the production of 30,000 to 35,000 tonnes per year.
